title: remaining gaps in ADDR_GENERIC
author: b02
headline: TWO NEW DEFECTS. (NEW-1) 9 of the 62 ADDR_GENERIC entries are structurally inert: keys.py:42 gates alph on len>=3 and keys.py:41 gates nums on ^DIGITS+$, and 0 of 62 entries is digit-only, so no sub-3-char entry can ever change a blocking key. They strip 39.91% of test-split removal mass. (NEW-2) the D116 IDF-cost argument does NOT transfer here: keys.py:39 filters a LOCAL list and keys.py:45 never returns atoks, so adding entries costs zero IDF feature mass.
units: all mass figures are TOKEN OCCURRENCES within the top-4000 listed addr_tokens per country per file, never rows

dictionary_shape.consequence_of_being_a_list: membership test only (pl.element().is_in(ADDR_GENERIC)); there are no key->value pairs, so the work order's 'distinct canonical values' question is not applicable, and an empty value that deletes a token - as ADDR_CANON_COMMON does for 15 keys and ADDR_CANON_FR for 5 - is not expressible. Every entry is a plain suppression key.
dictionary_shape.country_scoping: none - keys.py:39 has no country predicate

NEW_1_structurally_inert_entries.mechanism: toks (keys.py:39) has exactly two consumers: nums (keys.py:41, filter ^DIGITS+$) and alph (keys.py:42, filter len_chars>=3). make_keys (keys.py:53-73) consumes only tl.nums and tl.alph. A stoplist entry can therefore only matter if its canonical form is digit-only (-> nums) or at least 3 chars (-> alph).
NEW_1_structurally_inert_entries.claim_type: INFERENCE from quoted code filters; no pipeline run, no score delta claimed

NEW_2_idf_argument_does_not_transfer.d116_argument: For FR_REGIONS, normalize.py:333-335 'continue' skips toks.extend(ctoks) at :350, deleting tokens BEFORE prep.py:16 writes atoks, so extending the dictionary removes IDF feature mass.
NEW_2_idf_argument_does_not_transfer.why_it_fails_here: ADDR_GENERIC is applied at keys.py:39, which builds a LOCAL list. keys.py:45 returns only [rid, country, nt, pref, nums, alph, pin, fk] - atoks is NOT an output column and is never written back.
NEW_2_idf_argument_does_not_transfer.consequence: The 19-entry gap is NOT the regression D116's precedent suggests. Adding ADDR_GENERIC entries is a pure blocking-key cleanup with zero feature cost. The reason not to add all 19 is homogeneity, not IDF.
NEW_2_idf_argument_does_not_transfer.claim_type: code-path trace plus quoted select() list; no pipeline run

would_be_a_regression.reason: saint/sainte are genuine French toponym morphemes (Saint-Etienne, Sainte-Marie). Adding them to a DELETE stoplist strips a discriminative token from French blocking keys, making keys coarser and less selective. D091 called this an unmade design decision; 174895 is the number that makes it a decision worth not making blind.

rte_asymmetry_NEW.status: NEW framing of a token that was listed but not diagnosed
rte_asymmetry_NEW.description: rte is the canon output of route/rt (normalize.py:177) and FR route/rte (normalize.py:204). rte is NOT in ADDR_GENERIC. But rd IS, and rd is the canon output of road (normalize.py:155) - a semantically identical concept. The dictionary suppresses the English spelling and leaks the French one: the same inversion shape as ter/bis, but CROSS-COUNTRY rather than France-only.
rte_asymmetry_NEW.why_it_matters: adding rte alongside the existing rd costs nothing and closes all three countries at once
